questions.question: The cash budget forecasts:
options: The BANK BALANCE — expected receipts against payments, on the cash basis
Profit earned each month
Only credit sales
The value of closing stock

questions.question: A credit sale enters the projected income statement:
options: Only when the debtor pays
In the month the goods change hands — the accrual basis, paid or not
In the month after the sale
Never — credit sales are excluded

questions.question: Items appearing ONLY in the projected income statement include:
options: Drawings and loan repayments
Capital contributed by the owner
Depreciation, bad debts and the accrued portions of expenses
VAT paid over to the revenue service

questions.question: The sorting question to ask of every item in a question is:
options: Is the amount above R10 000?
Is the item recorded in the journal?
Does the item have a source document?
Does it move MONEY this month (cash budget), earn income or consume value this month (projected income statement), or both?

questions.question: With credit sales of R168 000 in May and 60% settling in the following month less a 5% discount, June collects from May:
options: R95 760 — 60% of R168 000 is R100 800, less the 5% discount
R100 800 — no discount applies

questions.question: June's collections from debtors draw on:
options: June's credit sales only
THREE earlier months' credit sales — May, April and March
The whole year's sales equally
Cash sales only

questions.question: The settlement discount is deducted:
options: From the full month's credit sales
From every collection in the month
ONLY from the prompt 60% portion that earns it
From cash sales as well

questions.question: The 5% of credit sales that is written off:
options: Reduces the receipts line of the cash budget
Appears as a payment in the cash budget
Is carried forward to the next quarter's collections
Never enters the cash budget — it appears in the projected income statement as bad debts

subtopics.title: Building the Cash Budget and the Projected Income Statement

questions.question: The cash budget's monthly chain runs:
options: Receipts less payments = surplus or deficit; plus opening balance = closing balance, which becomes next month's opening
Sales less cost of sales = gross profit
Income less expenses = net profit
Opening stock plus purchases less closing stock

questions.question: In the projected income statement, the sales figure for a month is:
options: Cash sales only
The FULL figure — cash and credit together — in the month of sale
Only the amounts collected from debtors
Sales spread across the three collection months

questions.question: A forecast closing bank balance that goes negative signals:
options: A calculation error by definition
That the business must be making a loss
A forecast OVERDRAFT — the most valuable early warning the document can give
That sales were recorded twice

questions.question: A complete answer to "how can one month show strong profit and a cash shortfall?" must:
options: State that one is cash and one is profit
Say the budget was prepared incorrectly
Recommend cutting expenses
NAME the timing gap and its items — credit sales collected later, stock paid earlier, an asset bought for cash

questions.question: A variance is stated fully by giving:
options: The item, both figures, the difference in rand and percentage, and favourable or unfavourable
Only the actual figure
Only the budgeted figure
A general remark about performance

questions.question: An expense UNDER budget is not automatically a victory because:
options: Favourable variances must be reversed
Advertising at half the plan may have caused the sales shortfall beside it, and postponed maintenance is next year's breakdown
Expenses are required to equal budget exactly
It proves the budget was padded

questions.question: Presenting a projection the preparer knows to be unreachable, in order to obtain a loan, is:
options: Healthy optimism
Standard negotiating practice
MISREPRESENTATION — a fraud on the lender
Acceptable if the loan is repaid

questions.question: What promotes a budget from a wish to a control is:
options: Printing it formally
Using conservative figures
Preparing it before the year starts
The monthly COMPARISON of actual against budget, with material variances explained

questions.question: The brother who washed R9 000 of cars but holds R6 000 shows that:
options: Earning well and holding money are two different, both-true answers about the same month
He priced his washes incorrectly
A third of his customers cheated him
Profit is imaginary

questions.question: Drawings, buying a delivery scooter and repaying a loan belong:
options: In the profit forecast only
In the CASH BUDGET — they move money even though they are not income or expenses
In neither forecast
Only in the year-end statements

questions.question: Depreciation belongs only in the profit forecast because:
options: It is too small to matter
It is settled once a year
The scooter wears out this month, but not one rand leaves the account because of the wearing
It is a kind of drawings

subtopics.title: Working Out What Will Actually Arrive

questions.question: Money landing in June comes from:
options: Sixty percent of May's credit sales, a quarter of April's, a tenth of March's — three months landing in one
June's credit sales only
An equal slice of every month of the year
Cash sales only

questions.question: With March, April and May credit sales of R112 000, R126 000 and R168 000, June's collection from debtors is:
The grid — sales down the side, arrival months across — exists because:
options: Answer books are printed as grids
Grids are quicker to add up
Three different months' selling lands in one month's bank account, and juggling that mentally tangles the strands
It replaces the cash budget entirely

questions.question: The five percent that never arrives is excluded from the cash budget because:
options: It is too small to record
It is collected by attorneys
It is deducted from the discount instead
You cannot plan to receive money that will not arrive — it belongs in the profit forecast as bad debts

subtopics.title: Profitable and Broke at the Same Time

questions.question: The shop's record month can empty its bank account because:
options: Stock was paid for in May, wages went out in June, a scooter was bought for cash, and the credit customers only pay in July
The sales were recorded in the wrong month
The profit calculation was wrong
The bank withheld the deposits

questions.question: "Profit measures whether the business deserves to survive; cash decides..."
options: The VAT owed
Whether it DOES — a business can absorb a poor profit month but not a payday with an empty account
The value of the stock
The mark-up percentage

questions.question: Seeing the squeeze in advance gives the owner cheap options such as:
options: Skipping the wage payment
Closing for the month
Postponing the scooter, arranging an overdraft early, tightening credit terms, or asking the supplier for longer payment
Doubling all prices at once

questions.question: Budgets get dressed up when:
options: Assumptions are written down openly
Actuals are compared every month
The delivery team drafts its own budget
Sales lines are inflated to win finance, or expense lines padded to bury later overspending
